title: Bloomberg：OpenAI 完成 110 亿美元融资首批到账，估值达 1.25 万亿美元
content:
Rohan Paul· @rohanpaul_ai · X·· 21 分钟前精选AI 评分86
AI 导读
据 Bloomberg，OpenAI 完成 110 亿美元新融资，这是估值 1.25 万亿美元一轮的首笔资金。投资者当日已打款，剩余部分总额最高 200 亿美元，预计数周内到账。
推荐理由
转引 Bloomberg 报道，给出本轮到账金额、整体估值和剩余资金节奏，可用于跟踪 OpenAI 融资进展。
正文 · 原文
Bloomberg: OpenAI closed $11B in a new funding, the first tranche of a round valuing it at $1.25T.
Investors had wired the cash today, and the rest, up to $20B in total, should follow within weeks.
来源：Rohan Paul · x.com

report.summary: Bloomberg reports OpenAI closed the first $11B tranche of a round valuing it at $1.25 trillion, with up to $20B total expected within weeks.
report.background: OpenAI has raised capital in ever-larger steps: roughly $13B from Microsoft since 2019, a $6.6B round at a $157B valuation in late 2024, and SoftBank-led commitments near $300B in early 2025, followed by employee share sales that pushed secondary pricing toward $500B. Each step up has tracked a jump in compute spending — the Stargate data-center program, multi-hundred-billion-dollar cloud contracts and chip deals with Nvidia and AMD. The company restructured into a public benefit corporation with a nonprofit foundation in control, clearing the way for conventional equity raises. Meanwhile the wider market has debated whether AI capex is outpacing revenue, making OpenAI's ability to keep pulling in private capital a bellwether for the whole sector.
key_points: The first tranche is cash in hand, not a pledge: Bloomberg says investors wired $11B on the day of the report, with the remainder of a round worth up to $20B expected to land within weeks. Speed of closing signals unusually strong demand.

The headline number is the valuation: $1.25 trillion would make OpenAI one of the most valuable private companies ever, roughly two and a half times the ~$500B level implied by secondary share sales reported earlier in 2025.

The article does not name the investors or disclose terms such as preference stack, liquidation rights or whether the round includes strategic partners paying in compute rather than cash — details worth watching for in follow-up filings and reporting.

The raise is best read as fuel for infrastructure: OpenAI has committed to enormous data-center and chip spending through Stargate and supplier deals, so fresh equity is largely pre-committed to compute rather than to free cash flow.

It is also a market signal. A trillion-dollar private valuation landing while pundits argue about an AI bubble suggests institutional appetite for frontier labs has not cooled, even as scrutiny of circular vendor-financing deals grows.
report.impact: For the AI industry, a $1.25T mark resets the ceiling for every frontier lab and gives OpenAI leverage in chip and cloud negotiations, while raising the bar for rivals who must now justify their own valuations against it. For developers, the practical effect is more capacity and likely more aggressive model releases, but also a supplier with deepening lock-in across APIs and cloud agreements — pricing and deprecation decisions will carry more weight. For regular users, expect continued rapid feature rollouts bundled into consumer subscriptions, alongside louder questions about whether these services will eventually be priced to recoup the capital. The main risk is concentration: one private company now anchors a large share of the sector's financing narrative.
report.tools: No open-source project is directly involved, but readers tracking this story can follow Bloomberg's deal coverage, Crunchbase and PitchBook for cap-table updates, and SEC or state corporate filings for the PBC entity. As a hedge against dependency on any single vendor, watch open-weight model releases (Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek) and self-hosting stacks such as vLLM, Ollama and LiteLLM, which let teams route workloads across providers.
